capture.final_message:
Use extensionality for simple graphs, viewing a graph through its adjacency relation—or equivalently its edge set in `Sym2 V`.

For the first conjunct, fix vertices `v w` and reduce both sides to adjacency of `v` and `w`. The useful intermediate equivalences are:

- adjacency in `fromEdgeSet s` means `s(v,w) ∈ s` together with the non-loop condition `v ≠ w`;
- adjacency in an infimum of graphs means adjacency in every component;
- membership in `⋂ i, f i` means membership in every `f i`.

Thus both sides become `v ≠ w ∧ ∀ i, s(v,w) ∈ f i`. This also handles the empty-index case: the intersection is universal and produces the complete graph, matching the empty infimum `⊤`.

For the second conjunct, unfold `incidenceSet`. The edge `s(v,w)` is incident to `v` automatically, so its membership reduces to membership in `G.edgeSet`; then use the standard characterization
` s(v,w) ∈ G.edgeSet ↔ G.Adj v w`.
The irreflexivity of adjacency accounts for the degenerate case `v = w`.
